name: Davis-Ray Ghost Neutrinos
description: A current of neutrinos along one axis of Taub's static plane symmetric vacuum, which Talmadge M. Davis and John R. Ray found in 1974. The neutrinos carry no energy or momentum, so the geometry around them is that of empty space, with a timelike singularity on one side.
convention: We keep factors of $c$ explicit, and the Ricci tensor is the standard contraction, $R_{\mu\nu} = R^\alpha{}_{\mu\alpha\nu}$.
history: A current of neutrinos runs along one axis of this spacetime, and the geometry around it is the geometry of empty space. Talmadge M. Davis and John R. Ray, of the Department of Physics and Astronomy at Clemson University, sent the solution to Physical Review on 12 October 1973, and it appeared on 15 January 1974 [davis1974]. It solves the Einstein-Dirac equations for neutrinos in a spacetime that is static and plane symmetric [davis1974]. The neutrino field is not zero, yet its energy momentum tensor vanishes, so the gravitational field is exactly that of vacuum [davis1974]. Davis and Ray called it a "ghost neutrino" field [davis1974].¶Neutrino fields of this kind had turned up a little earlier on gravitational waves. Jerry B. Griffiths identified a class of neutrino fields with zero energy momentum tensor and suggested that the spacetimes carrying them could also describe gravitational waves [pasic2014]. C. D. Collinson and P. B. Morris then showed that those spacetimes could be pp-waves or Robinson-Trautman solutions of type N [pasic2014, collinson1973]. The name ghost neutrinos came afterwards, from Davis and Ray [pasic2014]. In their example nothing depends on time, and the neutrinos flow at right angles to the planes of symmetry [davis1974].¶Empty space that is static and plane symmetric has one curved form, the vacuum Abraham Taub found in 1951 [taub1951, bedran1997]. With $L$ a length that sets the units of $t$, $x$, and $y$, its line element is $ds^2 = -(z/L)^{-2/3}c^2dt^2 + dz^2 + (z/L)^{4/3}(dx^2 + dy^2)$, and $L$ is no physical parameter, since rescaling $t$, $x$, and $y$ removes it [bedran1997]. The singularity at $z = 0$ is timelike, and every curvature invariant vanishes as $z$ grows [bedran1997]. M. L. Bedran, Mauricio O. Calvão, F. M. Paiva, and Ivano Damião Soares take Taub's spacetime to be the field outside a plane of negative mass, and a massive particle falling freely through it eventually recedes from the singularity, whatever its start [bedran1997]. Davis and Ray found in 1975 that their spacetime is of Petrov type D [davis1975plane].¶In Taub's coordinates the neutrino field is $\psi = (L/z)^{1/2}\chi$, with $\chi$ a constant spinor, and the massless Dirac equation holds for every constant $\chi$. The energy momentum tensor of this field vanishes when its current points along $z$, and that current is null, so the neutrinos stream at the speed of light toward the singularity or away from it. The neutrino flux $\sqrt{-g}\,j^z$ is the same constant on every plane of constant $z$. The density of the current falls as $1/z$, while the area of a patch of plane grows as $(z/L)^{4/3}$ and the static clocks run at the rate $(z/L)^{-1/3}$, and the three together hold the flux at one value.¶In January 1975 Davis and Ray let the plane symmetric ghost depend on time, and showed that a Lorentz transformation takes the time dependent current to the static one and a spinor transformation takes the wavefunction to the static wavefunction [davis1975plane]. The ghost current runs along geodesics that expand, and by earlier results their solution is the most general ghost of the Einstein-Dirac equations with an expanding current [davis1975plane]. In the same issue they put neutrinos in a static cylindrically symmetric spacetime with a radial current, and found that they can live there only where the spacetime is locally a static plane symmetric one [davis1975cylinder].¶J. Audretsch showed in 1976 that ghost neutrinos need an algebraically special spacetime, with the neutrino flux along a principal null direction of the Weyl tensor, so that the Kerr-Newman and the spherically symmetric spacetimes carry none [audretsch1976]. Griffiths showed in 1980 that ghost neutrino fields occur in Einstein-Cartan theory as well as in general relativity [griffiths1980]. In the first order formalism of Einstein-Cartan theory torsion adds to the canonical energy momentum of the neutrino, and there the ghost interpretation cannot be maintained [dereli2023].

related.text: At $\sigma = -1/2$ Levi-Civita's static cylinder is locally Taub's plane symmetric vacuum, the geometry the ghost neutrinos flow through [wang1997, taub1951].
The A III metric of Ehlers and Kundt is Taub's plane symmetric vacuum in other coordinates, the vacuum that carries the ghost neutrinos [martins1996, taub1951].

Continue Taub's coordinate $r$ through its singularity to negative values and the vacuum the ghost neutrinos flow through becomes Kasner's universe with exponents $(2/3, 2/3, -1/3)$, its singularity spacelike [bedran1997].
Massless Dirac fields again, with an electric field beside them, and here their energy holds a wormhole open [blazquez2021]. The ghost neutrinos are massless spinors that carry no energy.

coordinates.name: Taub

parameters.description: A length that sets the units of $t$, $x$, and $y$; rescaling them removes it, so Taub's vacuum has no physical parameter

coordinates.convention: We use Taub's coordinates $(t, x, y, z)$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time and $z$ the proper distance from the singularity. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter.

coordinates.name: Areal

parameters.description: A length that sets the units of $t$, $x$, and $y$; rescaling them removes it, so Taub's vacuum has no physical parameter

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, x, y, r)$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time and $r$ a length, $z = \tfrac{2}{3}L\left(r/L\right)^{3/2}$; $t$ is Taub's $t$ divided by $(2/3)^{1/3}$, and $x$ and $y$ are Taub's multiplied by $(2/3)^{2/3}$. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$.
